title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 5
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Tonnes of waste recycled last year and the number of collection rounds at five depots:

Ashwell: 2,860 tonnes, 44 rounds
Brigham: 4,130 tonnes, 71 rounds
Cotesby: 1,740 tonnes, 22 rounds
Dunwich: 3,520 tonnes, 66 rounds
Elverton: 2,210 tonnes, 31 rounds

Which depot recycled the most tonnes per round?
options: A. Ashwell
B. Brigham
C. Dunwich
D. Cotesby
E. Elverton
questions.explanation: Tonnes divided by rounds: Ashwell 65.0, Brigham 58.2, Cotesby 79.1, Dunwich 53.3, Elverton 71.3. Cotesby is highest. The depot recycling the most in total runs the most rounds and is not the most productive per round.

questions.prompt:
Annual patient referrals to a specialist clinic, in hundreds:

2021: 148
2022: 171
2023: 166
2024: 199
2025: 214

In which year was the percentage increase over the previous year greatest?
options: E. Referrals fell in every year
questions.explanation: Year on year: 2022 +15.5%, 2023 -2.9%, 2024 +19.9%, 2025 +7.5%. 2024 is largest at 19.9%. 2024 adds more referrals in absolute terms but from a larger base.

questions.prompt:
A shop's costs by category, as a share of the total:

Rent: 34%
Staff: 28%
Stock: 19%
Utilities: 8%
Insurance: 6%
Other: 5%

What is the smallest number of categories that together account for at least 70% of costs?
options: A. Two
B. Three
C. Four
D. Five
E. Six
questions.explanation: Largest first: 34 + 28 = 62%, short of 70. Adding Stock reaches 81%. So 3 categories are needed.

questions.prompt:
Two sites report their mean customer rating:

Site A: 120 responses, mean rating 4.6
Site B: 45 responses, mean rating 3.1

What is the mean rating across all responses?
questions.explanation: Weight by the number of responses: (120 × 4.6 + 45 × 3.1) / 165 = 4.19. Averaging the two site means gives 3.85, which is too low because the site with more responses scores higher.

questions.prompt:
Two payment processors:

Plan One: 8.5% of each transaction, no monthly fee
Plan Two: GBP 45.00 a month plus 2.5% of each transaction

Select the monthly turnover at which the two cost the same AND the cheaper plan at GBP 1,200.00 of monthly turnover.
options: A. GBP 500.00; Plan One is cheaper at GBP 1,200.00
B. GBP 750.00; Plan One is cheaper at GBP 1,200.00
C. GBP 750.00; Plan Two is cheaper at GBP 1,200.00
D. GBP 900.00; Plan Two is cheaper at GBP 1,200.00
E. The two never cost the same
questions.explanation: Equal when 0.085t = 45 + 0.025t, so t = 45/0.06 = GBP 750.00. At GBP 1,200.00: Plan One costs GBP 102.00, Plan Two costs GBP 75.00, so Plan Two is cheaper below the crossover.

questions.prompt:
Two product lines sold last month:

Line P: 300 units at GBP 18.00, unit cost GBP 6.40
Line Q: 180 units at GBP 26.00, unit cost GBP 9.10

Select the line contributing more total margin AND the line with the higher margin per unit.
options: A. Line P on total margin; Line Q on margin per unit
B. Line P on both measures
C. Line Q on total margin; Line P on margin per unit
D. Line Q on both measures
E. The two lines are equal on both measures
questions.explanation: Total margin: Line P GBP 3,480.00, Line Q GBP 3,042.00. Margin per unit: Line P GBP 11.60, Line Q GBP 16.90. Volume and unit margin point to different lines, which is why one figure alone cannot rank them.

questions.prompt:
A course provider has fixed costs of GBP 27,500.00 a year. Each place sells for GBP 165.00 and costs GBP 92.00 to deliver.

Select the number of places needed to break even AND the profit at 600 places.
options: A. 377 places; GBP 43,800.00
B. 377 places; GBP 16,300.00
C. 300 places; GBP 16,300.00
D. 377 places; GBP 20,000.00
E. 450 places; GBP 43,800.00
questions.explanation: Contribution is GBP 73.00 a place, so break-even is GBP 27,500.00 / GBP 73.00 = 377 places. At 600 places contribution totals GBP 43,800.00, less GBP 27,500.00 of fixed costs, leaving GBP 16,300.00.

questions.prompt:
Two heating systems, each with an installation cost and an annual running cost expressed as a percentage of that installation cost:

Option J: install GBP 3,400.00, running cost 11% of install a year
Option K: install GBP 5,200.00, running cost 6% of install a year

Select the cheaper system over 3 years AND the cheaper system over 8 years, counting installation plus running costs.
options: A. Option K at 3 years; Option K at 8 years
B. Option K at 3 years; Option J at 8 years
C. The two are equal at both horizons
D. Option J at 3 years; Option K at 8 years
E. Option J at 3 years; Option J at 8 years
questions.explanation: Over 3 years: Option J GBP 4,522.00, Option K GBP 6,136.00. Over 8 years: Option J GBP 6,392.00, Option K GBP 7,696.00. The cheaper installation wins over a short horizon and loses over a long one, because its running cost is the larger share.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): patient admissions last year — Ward 1 3,400, Ward 2 1,900, Ward 3 2,750

SOURCE 2 (table): recorded infections — Ward 1 26, Ward 2 11, Ward 3 22

SOURCE 3 (memo): "Infection control should be reviewed where the rate per admission is highest."

Which ward should be reviewed first on that criterion?
options: A. Ward 1
B. Ward 2
C. Ward 3
D. The three wards are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Infections per thousand admissions: Ward 1 7.6, Ward 2 5.8, Ward 3 8.0. Ward 3 is highest. Ward 1 records the most infections in total and also admits the most patients.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (memo): "Our repeat-purchase rate is 64%, well above the 45% industry figure, so our customers are unusually loyal."

SOURCE 2 (method note): "Repeat purchase is measured among customers who created an account; guest checkouts are excluded."

SOURCE 3 (table): 58% of orders are placed as guest checkouts.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. The company's customers are less loyal than the industry average
B. The industry figure is calculated the same way
C. Guest checkouts are placed by customers who never return
D. The 64% describes a minority of orders and cannot be compared with the industry figure without knowing how that is measured
E. Repeat purchase is not a useful measure of loyalty
questions.explanation: Account holders place 42% of orders, so the rate covers a minority, and Source 1's comparison assumes the industry figure uses the same base — which nothing here establishes. Option C asserts something about guests that the sources do not report.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): hours run last quarter — Machine A 620, Machine B 1,450, Machine C 890

SOURCE 2 (table): fault rate per hundred hours — Machine A 4.1, Machine B 1.8, Machine C 2.6

SOURCE 3 (email): "Each fault costs the same to attend, so rank the machines by number of faults."

Which machine generated the most faults?
options: A. Machine A
B. Machine B
C. Machine C
D. All three generated the same number
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Faults are hours multiplied by rate per hundred hours: Machine A 25.4, Machine B 26.1, Machine C 23.1. Machine B is highest. Machine A has the worst rate but runs least; Machine B has the best rate but runs most.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Absence fell from 4.8% to 3.9% of working days after the wellbeing programme began."

SOURCE 2 (table): absence across the sector fell from 4.7% to 3.8% over the same period.

SOURCE 3 (note): "The programme cost GBP 180,000.00 in its first year."

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. The programme's effect is at most about a tenth of a percentage point beyond the sector-wide fall
B. The programme reduced absence by 0.9 percentage points
C. The programme increased absence relative to the sector
D. Absence would have risen without the programme
E. The cost of the programme cannot be compared with any benefit
questions.explanation: The firm fell 0.9 points and the sector fell 0.9 points, so the difference attributable to the programme is roughly zero to one tenth of a point once rounding is allowed. Source 1 alone supports option B, which is why the sector comparison is the decisive source.

questions.prompt:
A cyclist rode from one town to another. What was her average speed?

(1) The journey took 90 minutes.
(2) She covered 36 km in 90 minutes.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives time with no distance. (2) gives both: 36 km in 1.5 hours is 24 km/h — sufficient on its own, and it also makes (1) redundant rather than necessary.

questions.prompt:
What is the area of a rectangular plot?

(1) Its perimeter is 84 m.
(2) Its length is 6 m greater than its width.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) allows many shapes with the same perimeter. (2) fixes the relationship but not the size. Together, 2(w + w + 6) = 84 gives w = 18 and length 24, so the area is 432 m².

questions.prompt:
A shop sold 150 tickets, some at GBP 12.00 and the rest at GBP 20.00. How many were sold at GBP 20.00?

(1) Takings were GBP 2,440.00.
(2) 70 tickets were sold at GBP 12.00.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1): if x sold at 20, then 12(150 - x) + 20x = 2440, so 1,800 + 8x = 2,440 and x = 80 - sufficient. From (2): 150 - 70 = 80 - also sufficient. The two statements agree, since 70 x 12 plus 80 x 20 is 2,440.

questions.prompt:
Is a certain integer n divisible by 6?

(1) n is divisible by 3.
(2) n is divisible by 4.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: Divisibility by 6 requires factors 2 and 3. (1) gives 3 but not 2; (2) gives 4, hence 2, but not 3. Together n has both 3 and 2, so it is divisible by 6 — sufficient only in combination.

questions.prompt:
Which branch handles the most orders per staff hour?

Branch | Orders | Staff hours (weekly) | Annual revenue | On-time rate
Alderney | 1,240 | 86 | GBP 412,000.00 | 92%
Bexford | 890 | 61 | GBP 318,000.00 | 88%
Caldon | 1,680 | 118 | GBP 505,000.00 | 79%
Denholm | 640 | 39 | GBP 233,000.00 | 95%
Ellingham | 1,075 | 74 | GBP 366,000.00 | 84%
Fennimore | 1,420 | 96 | GBP 448,000.00 | 81%
options: A. Alderney
B. Bexford
C. Caldon
D. Ellingham
E. Denholm
questions.explanation: Orders divided by staff hours: Alderney 14.42, Bexford 14.59, Caldon 14.24, Denholm 16.41, Ellingham 14.53, Fennimore 14.79. Denholm is highest. The branch with the most orders also has the most hours and is not the most efficient.

questions.prompt:
How many branches have an on-time rate below the mean on-time rate for the six?

Branch | Orders | Staff hours (weekly) | Annual revenue | On-time rate
Alderney | 1,240 | 86 | GBP 412,000.00 | 92%
Bexford | 890 | 61 | GBP 318,000.00 | 88%
Caldon | 1,680 | 118 | GBP 505,000.00 | 79%
Denholm | 640 | 39 | GBP 233,000.00 | 95%
Ellingham | 1,075 | 74 | GBP 366,000.00 | 84%
Fennimore | 1,420 | 96 | GBP 448,000.00 | 81%
options: A. One
B. Two
C. Three
D. Four
E. Five
questions.explanation: The mean on-time rate is (92 + 88 + 79 + 95 + 84 + 81) / 6 = 86.50%. Below it: Caldon 79%, Ellingham 84%, Fennimore 81% — 3 branches.

questions.prompt:
Which branch has the greatest number of late orders?

Branch | Orders | Staff hours (weekly) | Annual revenue | On-time rate
Alderney | 1,240 | 86 | GBP 412,000.00 | 92%
Bexford | 890 | 61 | GBP 318,000.00 | 88%
Caldon | 1,680 | 118 | GBP 505,000.00 | 79%
Denholm | 640 | 39 | GBP 233,000.00 | 95%
Ellingham | 1,075 | 74 | GBP 366,000.00 | 84%
Fennimore | 1,420 | 96 | GBP 448,000.00 | 81%
options: A. Alderney
B. Bexford
C. Denholm
D. Caldon
E. Ellingham
questions.explanation: Late orders are orders multiplied by the shortfall from 100%: Alderney 99, Bexford 107, Caldon 353, Denholm 32, Ellingham 172, Fennimore 270. Caldon is highest. The worst on-time rate belongs to Caldon, which is not the same branch.

questions.prompt:
Which branch ranks second highest on revenue per order?

Branch | Orders | Staff hours (weekly) | Annual revenue | On-time rate
Alderney | 1,240 | 86 | GBP 412,000.00 | 92%
Bexford | 890 | 61 | GBP 318,000.00 | 88%
Caldon | 1,680 | 118 | GBP 505,000.00 | 79%
Denholm | 640 | 39 | GBP 233,000.00 | 95%
Ellingham | 1,075 | 74 | GBP 366,000.00 | 84%
Fennimore | 1,420 | 96 | GBP 448,000.00 | 81%
options: A. Bexford
B. Alderney
C. Caldon
D. Denholm
E. Ellingham
questions.explanation: Revenue per order: Alderney GBP 332.26, Bexford GBP 357.30, Caldon GBP 300.60, Denholm GBP 364.06, Ellingham GBP 340.47, Fennimore GBP 315.49. Ranked highest first: Denholm, Bexford, Ellingham, Alderney, Fennimore, Caldon. Second is Bexford.
